\chapter{STEPSS in Python}\label{doc:py-overview}

\textbf{stepss} is the package that delivers \hyperref[ch-overview]{STEPSS in Python}, one of the platform's two editions. It provides an interface to the RAMSES dynamic simulator and the Helios AC power-flow engine, covering the full workflow: defining test cases, launching simulations, querying system states at runtime, extracting and plotting results, and running power flows. The package embeds pre-compiled RAMSES and Helios libraries for Windows, Linux, and macOS and exposes them through a clean Python API.

\texttt{stepss.cfg} & Defines a test case: data files, disturbance file, output files, observables, and runtime options. \\
\texttt{stepss.sim} & Runs simulations. Supports start/pause/continue, runtime queries, and disturbance injection. \\
\texttt{stepss.extractor} & Extracts and visualises time-series results from trajectory files produced by a simulation. \\
\texttt{stepss.monitor} & Plots chosen quantities while a simulation runs, one panel per observable. \\
\texttt{stepss.helios.HeliosSession} & Runs AC power flows with the Helios engine: load, modify with redispatch, solve, contingency screening, and file exports. \\
\end{longtable}\end{small}
}

\section{Platform Support}\label{py-overview:platform-support}

stepss supports Windows, Linux, and macOS for both dynamic simulation and power flows. All binaries are bundled directly in the package, no separate simulator installation is required. See the \hyperref[doc:py-install]{installation guide} for per-platform system prerequisites.
